articles.title: OpenAI Launches GPT-5 Turbo with Native Multimodal Reasoning Across Text, Image, Audio, and Video
articles.summary: OpenAI released GPT-5 Turbo, featuring deeply integrated multimodal reasoning that can jointly process text, images, audio, and video in a single inference pass rather than relying on modular adapters. Benchmarks show significant gains in complex cross-modal tasks such as video understanding and scientific diagram interpretation. The model also introduces a substantially larger context window and improved instruction-following fidelity.

articles.title: Google DeepMind's Gemini Ultra 2 Achieves State-of-the-Art on Mathematical Olympiad Problems
articles.summary: DeepMind announced Gemini Ultra 2, which scored above 90% on a curated set of International Mathematical Olympiad problems, surpassing previous AI systems by a wide margin. The model combines reinforcement learning over chain-of-thought traces with a novel formal verification loop that checks proof steps against Lean 4. Researchers highlight implications for automated theorem proving and AI-assisted scientific discovery.

articles.title: Tesla Optimus Gen 3 Begins Limited Deployment in Automotive Assembly Lines
articles.summary: Tesla has started deploying its third-generation Optimus humanoid robots in select Gigafactory assembly stations, handling tasks like parts bin picking, cable routing, and quality inspection. The Gen 3 units feature upgraded dexterous hands with 22 degrees of freedom and improved vision-language-action models enabling rapid task adaptation. Tesla reports that the robots achieve roughly 85% of human-equivalent throughput on targeted tasks after minimal demonstration-based training.

articles.title: Boston Dynamics and Hyundai Unveil Atlas Commercial Platform for Logistics Warehousing
articles.summary: Boston Dynamics officially launched the commercial Atlas platform tailored for large-scale warehousing and logistics, developed in partnership with Hyundai. The electric humanoid can autonomously navigate dynamic warehouse environments, manipulate irregular packages up to 25 kg, and coordinate with existing fleet management systems via a standardized ROS 2 interface. Early pilot customers include DHL and Amazon, with deployments beginning Q1 2027.

articles.title: Anthropic Introduces Constitutional AI 2.0 Framework with Real-Time Auditable Safety Constraints
articles.summary: Anthropic published its Constitutional AI 2.0 framework, which introduces machine-auditable safety constraints that can be inspected and formally verified in real time during inference. The system uses a lightweight constraint-satisfaction layer that runs alongside the main model, providing cryptographically signed compliance logs. The approach is positioned as a step toward regulatory-grade AI safety assurance for enterprise and government deployments.

articles.title: TSMC Begins Volume Production of 1.4nm Process Node, Powering Next-Gen AI Accelerators
articles.summary: TSMC confirmed volume production on its N1.4 process node at its Kaohsiung fab, targeting next-generation AI training and inference chips from major customers including NVIDIA and Apple. The node delivers approximately 25% improved performance-per-watt over the 2nm node, enabled by gate-all-around nanosheet transistors with backside power delivery. Industry analysts expect the first consumer and data-center products on N1.4 to ship in mid-2027.

articles.title: Microsoft and Atom Computing Demonstrate Logical Qubit Error Rates Below Fault-Tolerance Threshold
articles.summary: Microsoft and Atom Computing jointly announced a neutral-atom quantum computing prototype that sustains logical qubit error rates below 10⁻⁶ across a 48-logical-qubit register using real-time error correction. This crosses a key threshold for fault-tolerant quantum computation and validates Microsoft's topological-hybrid error correction codes in a scalable hardware platform. The teams project a path to 1,000+ logical qubits within two years.

articles.title: EU AI Act Enforcement Begins: First Compliance Audits Target Foundation Model Providers
articles.summary: The European Union's AI Office initiated its first formal compliance audits under the AI Act's general-purpose AI provisions, targeting major foundation model providers including OpenAI, Google, and Meta. Auditors are evaluating systemic risk assessments, training data documentation, and energy consumption disclosures required under the GPAI Code of Practice. The enforcement actions are being closely watched as a precedent for AI regulation worldwide.
